objective: Determine the primary mechanism causing a synthetic request-latency regression and justify the conclusion using at least two experiment/result cycles. Distinguish load-relief correlations from the causal mechanism.

starting_observations.observation: At concurrency 64, p95 latency is 412 ms and mean retries per request are 3.1.
Halving concurrency to 32 lowers p95 latency to 286 ms.
starting_observations.warning: This observation is real but may be non-discriminating.

starting_observations.observation: CPU utilization remains below 48% and queue occupancy never exceeds 62%.

candidate_hypotheses.statement: The regression is primarily queue-capacity saturation under concurrency.
Retry state is incorrectly retained across pooled request lifecycles, amplifying retries and latency.
Timeout timestamp quantization is causing retries to bunch into the same bucket.

experiment_catalog.intervention: Increase queue capacity by 4x while holding concurrency and retry policy fixed.
Disable connection-pool reuse while holding concurrency and retry policy fixed.
Explicitly reset retry state at each request boundary while leaving pool reuse enabled.
Replace quantized timeout timestamps with monotonic high-resolution timestamps.
Halve concurrency from 64 to 32 without changing any other mechanism.
